findings.issue_text: [BUG] The trailing `if` in `<%- end if %>` opens a new unterminated conditional (the template emits 4 `if/do` opens against only 3 `end`s), so best.html.erb compiles to syntactically invalid Ruby. ActionView raises a SyntaxError the first time the template is compiled: every /embed/best request for a URL with an existing topic — and every 30-second reload that loading.html.erb triggers once the retrieve job creates the topic — returns a 500 instead of the comments list, so the entire embed feature is dead on its success path; rspec-rails controller specs do not render views, so CI cannot catch it.

[BUG] TopicEmbed.import stores third-party feed/article HTML as the post raw with cook_method raw_html (which Post#cook returns verbatim), so the markup never passes through the normal Discourse Sanitize pipeline, and poll_feed even applies CGI.unescapeHTML to feed content, converting escaped entities into live tags. Whatever controls feed_polling_url content (or the arbitrary t[:link] URLs the disqus task fetches) gets stored XSS on the forum origin: script tags execute in the server-rendered embed iframe (framed with X-Frame-Options ALLOWALL), and event-handler attributes execute when forum users open the imported topic in the regular view.

[BUG] This spec asserts that the controller invokes TopicRetriever synchronously (`TopicRetriever.expects(:new)` / `retriever.expects(:retrieve)`), but the controller only enqueues the async Jobs::RetrieveTopic Sidekiq job (embed_controller.rb line 15), which never executes in-process in the test environment. The mocha expectations are never satisfied and the example fails with an unsatisfied-expectation error, leaving the diff's own suite red in CI and the controller→job→retriever wiring shipping with no passing test.

[BUG] TopicEmbed has no cleanup when its topic/post is destroyed, so deleting an imported topic leaves the topic_embeds row pointing at a destroyed topic: topic_id_for_embed feeds the dead id to TopicView.new, and the update branch does `PostRevisor.new(embed.post).revise!` on a nil post. After a staff member deletes a feed-imported topic (a routine anti-spam action), that URL's /embed/best raises Discourse::NotFound and serves an error in the iframe permanently — the retrieve job is never re-enqueued because topic_id is non-nil — and the next poll of changed content crashes with NoMethodError on nil in PostRevisor, killing the hourly feed job.

[BUG] poll_feed iterates rss.items with no per-item error handling inside a job declared `sidekiq_options retry: false`, and line 35 assumes every feed item exposes a `content` element (`i.content.scrub`), which standard RSS 2.0 description-only items do not. One malformed or content-less item raises NoMethodError, aborting the run at that item on this and every subsequent hourly invocation, so all items after it are never imported; with retry disabled the failure surfaces only in the sidekiq dead set, not to the admin who enabled feed polling.

[ADVISORY] feed_key (plus the `require 'digest/sha1'` that only serves it) is dead code: the "feed-modified:<sha1>" key it names is never written or read anywhere in the diff, and no If-Modified-Since/ETag conditional fetching exists. The next maintainer reading poll_feed assumes conditional-fetch throttling is implemented when the job actually refetches and re-parses the entire feed every hour; deleting the method and the require removes the false signal and the only use of digest/sha1 in the file.

[ADVISORY] import_remote — the open(url) fetch plus ruby-readability extraction with the tags/attributes whitelist that serves on-demand embedding, TopicRetriever's fetch_http fallback, and the disqus importer — is exercised by no test in the diff. A regression in the readability integration (whitelist option handling, title/content extraction, encoding failures) breaks the primary content-import path only at runtime inside background jobs, invisible to CI and to operators until embeds silently stay stuck on the loading page.

[ADVISORY] The import task removes the documented `-c/--category` method_option and all category wiring with no deprecation note, changing the task's public CLI surface. Operators running existing `thor disqus:import -c <category>` commands break: the value is no longer a known option so it is passed as a positional argument to a task that takes none and the invocation errors, and there is no longer any way to direct imports into a chosen category instead of Uncategorized.

[BUG] The new raw_html cook path returns raw HTML with no sanitization step anywhere in the import pipeline, silently dropping the 'untrusted HTML must be sanitized' requirement. Any markup in polled RSS/Atom item content (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 passes CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content) straight to TopicEmbed.import — over plain-HTTP fetches that are MITM-able and commonly carry comment/guest text), any readability-scraped attribute like href='javascript:…' (topic_embed.rb:48-50 whitelists tags but never filters URL schemes), and the embed_url interpolated raw into the imported_from footer at topic_embed.rb:13 (a quote in the URL breaks out of the single-quoted href) are all stored verbatim as post.cooked and rendered with `raw post.cooked` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19 and on the forum topic page — stored XSS in the forum origin for every visitor.

[BUG] poll_feed reads i.content on every feed item with no presence check or per-item error handling, so the first item without a content element aborts the entire feed poll. For an RSS 2.0 feed whose items carry only <description> (no content:encoded) or an Atom feed using <summary>, i.content is nil and nil.scrub raises NoMethodError mid-loop; with sidekiq_options retry: false the job dies at that item on every hourly run, so no items after it are ever imported and feed polling is permanently stalled — and spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb only stubs the flag gating, never the loop body, so nothing detects it.

[BUG] topic_id_for_embed and TopicEmbed.import match embed URLs by exact string with no canonicalization, so the same article reached via two spellings of its URL creates two topics. When the RSS item link and the discourseEmbedUrl the site owner configures differ by scheme (http vs https), trailing slash, or query string (utm params, ?p=123 style permalinks — all common), the lookup misses, the controller enqueues RetrieveTopic again, and a second TopicEmbed plus second topic is created for the same article, permanently splitting the discussion across duplicates.

[BUG] TopicEmbed has no lifecycle handling: nothing in the diff removes the row when its topic or post is deleted, and the update path dereferences embed.post with no nil guard. After a moderator deletes an imported topic (posts cascade, the topic_embeds row survives), every embed/best request for that article calls TopicView.new on a nonexistent topic_id and 500s inside the site's comment box forever; and when that article's content next changes, the hourly PollFeed hits embed.post == nil and PostRevisor.new(nil) raises NoMethodError on nil.raw, killing the whole feed job every run.

[BUG] ensure_embeddable hard-fails on any request whose browser sends no Referer, with no fallback validation of the embed request. Visitors using privacy extensions, corporate proxies that strip Referer, or referrer-policy-suppressing setups get Discourse::InvalidAccess (a 403 error page) rendered inside the comment box on every view of every embedded article, with no way for the site owner to serve them; this client population is entirely unaddressed.

[BUG] absolutize_urls treats protocol-relative URLs (//host/path) as root-relative and rewrites them into broken host-prefixed paths. href/src values in the era-standard protocol-relative form ('//cdn.example.com/img.png' — start_with?('/') matches and sub(/^\/+/, '') strips both slashes) become 'http://blog.com/cdn.example.com/img.png', so any feed or scraped article using protocol-relative links renders with permanently broken images and links in the embedded topic.

[ADVISORY] The only spec for the found-topic path mocks TopicView to return nil and no spec renders any embed view, so the feature's core acceptance criterion — which posts the embed actually shows — is never verified. The suite passes with @topic_view set to the mock's nil (best.html.erb:2 would NoMethodError on nil.posts if views rendered, and render_views is off), so TopicView's real handling of the {best: 5} option, the post selection, and the entire rendered output ship untested; a regression in any of them is invisible to CI.

[ADVISORY] The spec titled 'is 404 without an embed_url' asserts only response.should_not be_success, never the 404 status it promises. params.require(:embed_url) actually raises ActionController::ParameterMissing (surfacing as a 400/500, not a 404) and the assertion passes anyway, so the named acceptance criterion is unverified and any error status — including a 500 — is accepted as green.

[ADVISORY] The loading view reloads every 30 seconds unconditionally and the retrieval pipeline has no terminal failure state or retry budget. When import permanently fails (source article 404s, embed_by_username user is missing, content is unparseable), every visitor's browser reloads the iframe twice a minute forever — continuous request load from every embedded page, no user-visible failure message, and no operator signal that anything is broken.

[ADVISORY] embeddable_host is stored as free text with no validation or normalization while every code path compares it to the exact downcased URI host. An admin who enters 'http://myblog.com', 'myblog.com/', or a capitalized host makes every embed request fail the referer check with a 403 and no diagnostic anywhere — all embeds silently never work and nothing in the UI or logs explains why.

[ADVISORY] feed_key is defined and never called — dead code left over from a dropped skip-unchanged-feed requirement. The intended conditional-fetch check was silently dropped, so every hourly run (and every retrieve-triggered run inside TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve) re-parses the entire feed and re-processes every item, and the next reader must reverse-engineer whether feed_key was supposed to gate something.

[ADVISORY] The migration creates topic_embeds with force: true, and the PR also retrofits force: true into the already-shipped create_top_topics migration. In any environment where the table already holds rows when this migration runs (restored backup, re-baselined schema_migrations), create_table force silently drops all embed data; and editing the shipped top_topics migration means already-deployed databases never receive the change while fresh ones do, diverging environments.

[ADVISORY] The header conditional is closed with `<%- end if %>`, which only parses because ERB makes the next emitted text append the modifier's condition (an always-truthy buffer-append guard). The next person to edit this template — inserting a code-only tag, or removing the following blank line and text — changes the guard's condition or breaks the file's Ruby at compile time, turning every embed/best render into a 500; no reader can tell this line is load-bearing on what follows it.

[ADVISORY] PostRevisor accepts new raw but never touches cook_method, so staff edits to imported raw_html posts are saved without ever being cooked. A moderator who edits an imported article through the standard editor gets their markdown rendered verbatim as source text (Post#cook returns raw unchanged for raw_html posts), visibly breaking the post after a routine moderation action with no UI path to fix it.

[ADVISORY] The raw_html early return skips Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook), silently making a public plugin API conditional on cook_method. Any plugin registering an after_post_cook filter (transforms, sanitizers) never runs on imported posts — exactly the posts most likely to carry untrusted HTML — so plugin users get silent behavior divergence with no error or warning.

[ADVISORY] Every best request for an unknown embed_url enqueues a RetrieveTopic job with no enqueue-side dedup; the 60-second throttle lives only inside the job. A popular article whose import keeps failing (or before the first job runs) enqueues one Sidekiq job per page view, flooding the queue with no-op jobs that each still hit Redis and the database.

[ADVISORY] embed.js concatenates discourseUrl + 'embed/best' with no trailing-slash normalization and no validation of the configured variable. A site owner who sets discourseUrl without the trailing slash gets iframe src 'http://forum.example.comembed/best' — a 404 that renders as a silently blank comment box with no error surfaced to diagnose the misconfiguration.

[ADVISORY] The iframe height is measured exactly once at window.onload and never re-measured, while the iframe is created with scrolling='no'. Posts containing images that load after onload (or any late layout shift) grow the document past the single reported height, and the overflow is permanently clipped with no scrollbar — readers lose the bottom of the discussion on any embed with unsized images.

[BUG] Post#cook returns `raw` completely unfiltered when cook_method is raw_html, bypassing both the Markdown/sanitize pipeline and the Plugin::Filter :after_post_cook hook, so the invariant every Discourse render surface relies on — that `cooked` HTML was sanitized at cook time — is not enforced for imported posts. RSS item bodies (re-armed by CGI.unescapeHTML at poll_feed.rb:35, which converts <script> back to <script>) and readability-scraped embeddable-host pages (which routinely include visitor UGC) are stored as `cooked` with zero sanitization and rendered via `raw post.cooked` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19 and on regular topic pages — a malicious or compromised feed executes stored XSS in the Discourse origin and steals sessions of logged-in users viewing the topic or the embed iframe.

[BUG] TopicEmbed.import interpolates the embed_url directly into HTML — `"#{url}"` — after only a scheme-prefix regex check (`^https?://`), splicing the unescaped URL into post content that the new raw_html cook path stores and renders without any sanitization. A feed item link (or Disqus thread link, or embeddable-host URL) containing quotes or angle brackets, e.g. `http://host/x'>`, becomes live script in the 'Imported from' footer of a raw_html post — stored XSS in the forum origin — and even benign URLs containing an apostrophe corrupt the rendered footer.

[BUG] poll_feed reads `i.content` unconditionally, but RSS 2.0 items carry their text in `description` and need not have any `content` element, so SimpleRSS yields no such method (or nil, making `.scrub` fail) and the loop raises NoMethodError on the first item, before anything is imported. With `sidekiq_options retry: false` the entire hourly poll is discarded, so an operator who points the advertised 'RSS/ATOM feed' polling at a standard description-only RSS feed gets zero imports and no surfaced error — only a dead job in Sidekiq's log that repeats every hour.

[BUG] This embed-feature PR modifies the previously shipped CreateTopTopics migration to add `force: true` to `create_table :top_topics`, a change traceable to no requirement anywhere in the diff. Any `rake db:migrate:redo` (or re-run of the migration against a database where top_topics exists) now silently DROPs top_topics with all its computed score data and recreates it empty — a dev-convenience flag leaked into a destructive edit of an unrelated, already-applied migration.

[BUG] The diff rewrites the existing Disqus importer — deleting the documented `--category/-c` option, dropping the `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` propagation, and replacing the unconditional PostCreator topic creation with `TopicEmbed.import_remote` — work traceable to no embed-URL requirement. Operators re-running `thor disqus:import -c Foo` hit an unknown-option error; all re-imports lose their original post dates and category placement; and any thread whose link is not an http(s) URL or whose page fetch fails now silently produces no topic at all where the old code always created one.

[ADVISORY] The only requester validation on the public /embed/best endpoint is a client-supplied, trivially spoofable Referer host check, with no rate limiting or authentication before `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`, so the intended invariant — that only the embeddable site can trigger embedding — is not enforced against any non-browser client. Anyone on the internet sending `Referer: http://<embeddable_host>/` can enqueue a background fetch per request for unlimited distinct URLs on the configured host (query-string variants each get their own 60s throttle key in TopicRetriever), creating unbounded spam topics attributed to the embed user and flooding the Sidekiq queue.

[ADVISORY] The loading view reloads unconditionally every 30 seconds and the retrieval pipeline implements no terminal error state — fetch_http silently returns when embed_by_username is unset (topic_retriever.rb:50) and import_remote raises inside a retrying job — so an embed whose URL can never be imported never stops 'loading'. Every visitor to a permanently failing embed (deleted page, misconfigured embed_by_username, host/URL mismatch) is trapped in an infinite 'Loading Discussion...' loop that re-hits /embed/best and re-enqueues retrieve_topic jobs every 30 seconds per visitor indefinitely, with no signal to the operator that embedding is broken.

[ADVISORY] Embed identity is an exact-string match on embed_url with no canonicalization (query strings, trailing slashes, scheme variants), so the one-topic-per-article invariant is not enforced across different representations of the same URL. When the RSS item link (e.g. carrying utm tracking, pervasive in feeds) differs in any character from the blog page's discourseEmbedUrl, poll_feed creates one topic, the embed lookup misses it, and retrieve_topic's import_remote creates a second topic for the same article — splitting the discussion and duplicating content with no code path to reconcile them.

[ADVISORY] TopicEmbed rows have no lifecycle coupling to their topic or post (no dependent-destroy, no deletion hook anywhere in the diff), so the normal staff action of deleting an imported topic strands the embed row and its stale topic_id/post references. After staff delete an imported (e.g. spam) topic, the blog embed for that URL breaks permanently — topic_id_for_embed returns the dead id and TopicView.new raises RecordNotFound in the iframe — and the next feed update calls PostRevisor.new(embed.post) with a nil post, crashing the hourly job with NoMethodError until someone deletes the row by hand in SQL.

[ADVISORY] The embed script is added to the asset tree with no route, no precompile registration, and no reference from any manifest or view in this diff, so nothing ships that makes embed.js retrievable by a third-party site in a production deployment. An operator who configures the new embedding settings cannot actually deploy the feature end-to-end — embed.js is absent from the precompiled asset manifest and 404s in production, and the diff contains no embed-code snippet or docs for site owners, leaving the new settings inert.

[ADVISORY] perform_retrieve synchronously executes the entire scheduled feed poll inline (`Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`) on every retrieval miss, fetching and re-processing the whole feed to serve a single-URL request — implementation work not traceable to the 'retrieve this URL' requirement. With feed polling enabled, each first visit to any not-yet-imported page turns the retrieve_topic worker into a full feed fetch+parse+import cycle (in addition to the hourly schedule), so a slow or large feed multiplies worker latency and load scales with the number of distinct embedded pages.

[ADVISORY] `feed_key` builds a `feed-modified:` Redis key that nothing in the diff ever calls — a leftover from an abandoned conditional-fetch design, traceable to no requirement. Maintainers must reason about a caching layer that does not exist — the method implies feed polling is deduped when the whole feed is in fact re-fetched and every item re-processed each run — and deleting the three lines changes zero behavior.

[ADVISORY] The job opens with `require_dependency 'email/sender'`, a copy-paste leftover from a mail-sending job; nothing in RetrieveTopic or TopicRetriever touches email. Every worker that loads this job also boots the mailer stack for nothing, and readers are misled into thinking topic retrieval involves email; removing the line changes nothing.

[ADVISORY] The diff's new non-trivial parsing logic — poll_feed's link/id fallback and entity unescaping, TopicEmbed.import_remote's readability extraction, and the entire RetrieveTopic job body — has zero test coverage: poll_feed_spec stubs `poll_feed` in every example, topic_embed_spec never calls import_remote, and no spec exercises Jobs::RetrieveTopic. A regression in exactly the lines that handle untrusted feed input (the unescape/cook path where the stored-XSS risk lives) or in the Atom id fallback ships without any failing test, surfacing only as production job failures on operators' feeds.

[ADVISORY] The spec for Jobs::PollFeed opens with `require_dependency 'jobs/regular/process_post'` — an unrelated job file — so the subject constant resolves only through incidental Jobs autoload machinery rather than anything this require provides. Renaming or removing process_post breaks poll_feed_spec with a mystifying LoadError, and the next reader assumes a dependency between feed polling and post processing that does not exist.

[ADVISORY] The header if/else is closed with `<%- end if %>`, leaving a dangling `if` modifier that binds the next statement ERB emits after the block (the output on lines 7-8) as the block's condition, so the header renders only because that expression happens to be truthy. Any edit that reorders, removes, or wraps the following output line — or makes it falsy — silently stops the 'Discussion Highlights' header from rendering: a misparse trap invisible in the template source that no spec pins, since controller specs never render the view.

[ADVISORY] absolutize_urls rewrites only href/src values that begin with a single `/`, leaving protocol-relative (`//cdn.host/img.png`) and bare-relative (`img/foo.png`) URLs untouched in a PR whose stated subject is embed URL handling. Imported topics and embed views show broken images and dead links for feeds and pages that use protocol-relative or nested-relative paths — common on CDN-backed sites — with no signal to the operator explaining why the imported content renders broken.

[BUG] PostCreator now reads the render-pipeline bypass flag cook_method out of its public opts bag — the same bag Discourse's HTTP-facing post/topic creation endpoints populate from request params — so any logged-in user can submit cook_method=2 and have Post#cook return their raw HTML verbatim as `cooked`, skipping the markdown+sanitize pipeline (and the after_post_cook plugin filters). Arbitrary unsanitized HTML (including <script> tags) is persisted in `cooked` and rendered with `raw post.cooked` in topic views and the new embed iframe, giving any registered user a stored script-injection channel that the entire rendering architecture was built to prevent; a trusted-internal flag was welded onto a request-reachable constructor.

[BUG] poll_feed iterates rss.items with no per-item error isolation while `sidekiq_options retry: false` disables redelivery: an item lacking a content element (plain RSS 2.0 feeds use <description>, not <content:encoded>, leaving i.content nil so `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError), an item with a nil title (PostCreator inserts NULL against topics.title NOT NULL), or a previously-imported item whose post was deleted (PostRevisor.new(nil)) all raise inside the loop and abort the entire run. The first failing feed item kills every hourly poll at the same position each run (feeds are newest-first), so all articles below it are never imported — feed ingestion silently halts site-wide until the offending item rotates out of the feed, and with retry: false nothing ever reports or retries the loss.

[BUG] perform_retrieve calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously with no error isolation before falling through to fetch_http, so any exception from the inline whole-feed fetch/import (feed_polling_url 404ing, timing out, or returning malformed XML, or any per-item import failure) propagates out of the retrieve job before the HTTP fallback can run. With feed_polling_enabled and a broken feed URL, every retrieve_topic job dies inside the inline poll and fetch_http is never reached, so embeds for all articles are stuck in the 'Loading Discussion' reload loop forever; additionally, one blog pageview's job synchronously imports topics for the entire feed backlog, coupling a per-URL retrieval to a site-wide import with no boundary between them.

[BUG] TopicEmbed rows have no lifecycle coupling to their topic or post (no dependent-hook anywhere in this diff, no FK or cascade in the migration, and no deletion path for embed records at all), and the update branch dereferences embed.post unconditionally (`PostRevisor.new(post)` on a post whose row can be gone). When an admin deletes an imported topic or post, the topic_embeds row survives as an orphan: EmbedController#best keeps getting the dead topic_id from topic_id_for_embed, TopicView.new raises, and the article's iframe 500s on every pageview forever with no self-heal (the orphan row also blocks re-import), while the next feed poll crashes in PostRevisor.new(nil).revise! — a NoMethodError on nil that halts the batch.

[BUG] An embed's identity is exact string equality on embed_url with no canonicalization on either producer path: the RSS poll stores the feed's item link (commonly carrying utm query params, feedburner redirect hosts, or a trailing slash that differ from the live page URL) while the retrieve path stores whatever discourseEmbedUrl string the blog template supplies. The same article gets two topics: the scheduled poll imports the feed-link variant, then the first pageview's lookup misses, the retrieve job re-runs the poll (still missing, since the stored key differs by a query string or slash), and fetch_http creates a second topic under the page URL — discussion splits between two topics and the feed keeps updating the twin that no visitor ever sees.

[BUG] absolutize_urls only rewrites href/src values starting with '/' and uses `href.sub(/^\/+/, '')`, which strips BOTH leading slashes of protocol-relative URLs, mangling `//cdn.example.com/img.png` into `http://blog.example.com/cdn.example.com/img.png` (while bare relative paths like `img/foo.png` are left unabsolutized entirely). Imported articles using protocol-relative asset URLs — the standard pattern for CDN images and links in feeds — render broken images and dead links inside the embedded post, and the corrupted absolute URLs are persisted into the topic's raw and cooked.

[BUG] retrieved_recently? writes the 60-second throttle with two separate redis calls (`$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by `$redis.expire`) instead of an atomic SET-with-TTL, so a worker kill or connection drop between the two leaves `retrieved:<url>` with no expiry. That embed_url is then throttled forever — every subsequent retrieve_topic job returns at the throttle check, the page is never fetched or imported, and the blog shows the 'Loading Discussion' reload loop indefinitely with nothing indicating that a stale redis key is the cause.

[ADVISORY] embeddable_host is a free-text site setting compared against the bare host extracted by URI(...).host in both ensure_embeddable and TopicRetriever#invalid_host?, with no normalization or validation of the stored value anywhere. An operator who enters 'http://blog.example.com' or 'blog.example.com/' (the natural way to fill a field described only as a host) permanently fails the referer check on every embed request and invalid_host? on every retrieve — every iframe errors and no embed ever imports, with no message indicating the value's format is the cause.

[ADVISORY] fetch_http silently returns when embed_by_username is blank or names a nonexistent user, and the entire retrieve path (controller enqueue → job → retriever → import) emits no log line or error anywhere, while EmbedController's guard validates embeddable_host but never embed_by_username. A missing or mistyped embed_by_username produces a completely silent failure: every blog pageview enqueues a job that no-ops, the loading template reloads every 30 seconds forever, and the operator has no diagnostic to distinguish misconfiguration from slowness.

[ADVISORY] feed_key builds a `feed-modified:<sha1>` redis cache key that no code in this diff ever reads or writes, indicating an unfinished conditional-fetch optimization that was never wired in. Readers assume feed caching exists when every hourly run actually re-fetches and re-processes the entire feed (one TopicEmbed SELECT per item, plus a full HTTP fetch); as shipped it is dead code that misdocuments behavior — delete the method or wire it up.

[ADVISORY] The rewritten Disqus import replaces `PostCreator.new(..., created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), category: category_id)` with `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, whose opts only forwards :title and whose TopicEmbed.import path never accepts or forwards created_at. Every Disqus thread re-imported with this task is timestamped 'now' — the chronological order of the migrated forum is destroyed (all topics sort as brand-new and original posting dates are unrecoverable), and the previously supported :category option was dropped with no replacement.

[ADVISORY] The update branch revises only the post's raw body (PostRevisor#revise! receives new_raw and nothing else) and never revises the topic's title, so a retitle in the feed propagates the content change but not the headline. A blog that renames an article keeps a Discourse topic whose title and URL slug reflect the old headline forever — the change-tracking design (content_sha1) detects that the article changed but applies only half the change, so the embedded discussion diverges from the source it mirrors.

[BUG] Line 6 closes the header conditional with `<%- end if %>`, which compiles to the Ruby fragment `end if` with no condition expression and therefore fails ERB template compilation with a syntax error. Every /embed/best request that finds a topic raises ActionView::Template::Error when the template is compiled, so after loading.html.erb's 30-second reload swaps in the populated view the embed iframe serves an error page on every embedding site — the feature never renders comments; the new embed_controller_spec never renders views (no render_views), so CI stays green while the shipped artifact is dead.

[BUG] Post#cook returns raw completely unsanitized when cook_method is raw_html, bypassing the Discourse cooking/sanitization pipeline that every other post must pass through — the platform's core accepted security constraint. HTML fetched from the embedded host is stored and served as live markup: poll_feed passes i.content straight through with only CGI.unescapeHTML (which also re-materializes escaped entities into active tags) and no tag/attribute filtering, so a script/iframe/onerror payload in the feed content executes on the Discourse origin in every viewer's session — including staff — in both the topic page and the `raw post.cooked` embed view.

[BUG] The imported-from footer interpolates url into single-quoted HTML with only a `^https?://` regex guard, so a quote in the URL path escapes the href attribute (HTML5 tokenization starts a new attribute even without whitespace). An attacker who can place a link on the embedding host (e.g. a blog comment linking to /embed/best?embed_url=http://host/?s='onclick='...) supplies a referer that passes the embeddable_host check and an embed_url whose host passes TopicRetriever's host check while its query string carries the payload; the resulting raw_html post stores the injected event-handler attribute and executes on the Discourse origin when the topic is viewed.

[BUG] The Disqus import task deletes the documented `--category`/`-c` option and the category lookup, so imported threads can no longer be targeted at a category. Operators running the previously-accepted `disqus:import --category X` invocation either hit an unknown-option failure or have the flag silently ignored, landing every imported thread in Uncategorized with no replacement path anywhere in this diff.

[BUG] The rewritten import replaces PostCreator.new(..., created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), category: category_id) with TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title]), dropping the original thread timestamp for the first post. Imported OP posts carry the import-run timestamp while the unchanged reply loop keeps original Disqus dates, producing topics whose first post is dated after its replies and destroying the chronological fidelity the importer existed to preserve; the post body also changes from a permalink pointer to a full remote-page scrape with no acceptance of that content change.

[BUG] TopicEmbed declares belongs_to :topic and belongs_to :post with no dependent-destroy, callback, or cleanup path anywhere in this diff, so deleting an imported topic leaves the TopicEmbed row dangling. Staff deleting an imported topic (normal moderation) permanently breaks that URL's embed — topic_id_for_embed returns the dead topic_id and TopicView.new raises in the widget forever — and the next feed update whose content changed calls PostRevisor.new(embed.post) on nil, raising NoMethodError inside the hourly poll (sidekiq retry: false) and wedging feed import at that item while later items never import.

per_golden_matches.matched_candidate: [BUG] poll_feed reads `i.content` unconditionally, but RSS 2.0 items carry their text in `description` and need not have any `content` element, so SimpleRSS yields no such method (or nil, making `.scrub` fail) and the loop raises NoMethodError on the first item, before anything is imported. With `sidekiq_options retry: false` the entire hourly poll is discarded, so an operator who points the advertised 'RSS/ATOM feed' polling at a standard description-only RSS feed gets zero imports and no surfaced error — only a dead job in Sidekiq's log that repeats every hour.
per_golden_matches.reasoning: The candidate flags that `poll_feed` reads `i.content` unconditionally, and that many RSS 2.0 feeds use `description` without a `content` element, leading to `nil`/missing method and `.scrub` raising `NoMethodError`. This is the same core issue as the golden comment and implies the same fix (fallback to `description`).

per_golden_matches.golden_comment: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
per_golden_matches.matched_candidate: [BUG] The layout echoes the fully client-controlled request.referer into a single-quoted inline JavaScript string literal using only ERB HTML-escaping, which leaves single quotes intact, while the only upstream filter (embed_controller.rb:26 URI host check) accepts quote and paren characters in the path because they are RFC2396 mark characters. A request whose Referer is http://<embeddable_host>/');payload// passes the host check and renders the payload outside the string literal in the embed/loading page, executing attacker JS in the Discourse origin for whoever loads the framed embed — reflected XSS via a request header.
per_golden_matches.reasoning: The candidate issue describes the unescaped/insufficiently escaped request.referer header being embedded into an inline JavaScript string, allowing quote-breaking and reflected XSS. This is the same underlying vulnerability as the golden comment (referer header interpolated into JS without proper escaping leading to XSS).

per_golden_matches.golden_comment: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The trailing `if` in `<%- end if %>` opens a new unterminated conditional (the template emits 4 `if/do` opens against only 3 `end`s), so best.html.erb compiles to syntactically invalid Ruby. ActionView raises a SyntaxError the first time the template is compiled: every /embed/best request for a URL with an existing topic — and every 30-second reload that loading.html.erb triggers once the retrieve job creates the topic — returns a 500 instead of the comments list, so the entire embed feature is dead on its success path; rspec-rails controller specs do not render views, so CI cannot catch it.

[BUG] TopicEmbed.import stores third-party feed/article HTML as the post raw with cook_method raw_html (which Post#cook returns verbatim), so the markup never passes through the normal Discourse Sanitize pipeline, and poll_feed even applies CGI.unescapeHTML to feed content, converting escaped entities into live tags. Whatever controls feed_polling_url content (or the arbitrary t[:link] URLs the disqus task fetches) gets stored XSS on the forum origin: script tags execute in the server-rendered embed iframe (framed with X-Frame-Options ALLOWALL), and event-handler attributes execute when forum users open the imported topic in the regular view.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces a `raw_html` cook path that bypasses normal cooking/sanitization: `Post#cook` returns `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/post.rb). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and sets `raw` to feed/article HTML (`absolutize_urls(url, contents)`), with no sanitization step (app/models/topic_embed.rb). `Jobs::PollFeed` further calls `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, which can turn escaped entities back into live markup before importing (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb). The embed rendering uses `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb), so any injected tags/attributes in imported content would be rendered/executed. This is a verifiable XSS risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] This spec asserts that the controller invokes TopicRetriever synchronously (`TopicRetriever.expects(:new)` / `retriever.expects(:retrieve)`), but the controller only enqueues the async Jobs::RetrieveTopic Sidekiq job (embed_controller.rb line 15), which never executes in-process in the test environment. The mocha expectations are never satisfied and the example fails with an unsatisfied-expectation error, leaving the diff's own suite red in CI and the controller→job→retriever wiring shipping with no passing test.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when no `topic_id` is found it enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `loading`; it does not instantiate `TopicRetriever` or call `retrieve` synchronously. However, `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` explicitly sets `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)` and `retriever.expects(:retrieve)` in the no-embed case, so those expectations will not be met by the controller action shown in the diff, making the spec fail (red suite).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] TopicEmbed has no cleanup when its topic/post is destroyed, so deleting an imported topic leaves the topic_embeds row pointing at a destroyed topic: topic_id_for_embed feeds the dead id to TopicView.new, and the update branch does `PostRevisor.new(embed.post).revise!` on a nil post. After a staff member deletes a feed-imported topic (a routine anti-spam action), that URL's /embed/best raises Discourse::NotFound and serves an error in the iframe permanently — the retrieve job is never re-enqueued because topic_id is non-nil — and the next poll of changed content crashes with NoMethodError on nil in PostRevisor, killing the hourly feed job.

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `TopicEmbed` is introduced with `belongs_to :topic` / `:post` but no `dependent:` behavior and the migration adds no foreign keys/cascades, so deleting a topic/post will not remove the `topic_embeds` row. `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` (`pluck(:topic_id).first`) will still return the deleted topic id, and `EmbedController#best` will then call `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)` instead of enqueuing `:retrieve_topic`, leading to a persistent broken embed for that URL. Separately, in `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path does `post = embed.post` and then `PostRevisor.new(post)` when content changes; if the post was deleted, `embed.post` is `nil` and this will raise (consistent with the finding’s described crash).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] poll_feed iterates rss.items with no per-item error handling inside a job declared `sidekiq_options retry: false`, and line 35 assumes every feed item exposes a `content` element (`i.content.scrub`), which standard RSS 2.0 description-only items do not. One malformed or content-less item raises NoMethodError, aborting the run at that item on this and every subsequent hourly invocation, so all items after it are never imported; with retry disabled the failure surfaces only in the sidekiq dead set, not to the admin who enabled feed polling.

[ADVISORY] feed_key (plus the `require 'digest/sha1'` that only serves it) is dead code: the "feed-modified:<sha1>" key it names is never written or read anywhere in the diff, and no If-Modified-Since/ETag conditional fetching exists. The next maintainer reading poll_feed assumes conditional-fetch throttling is implemented when the job actually refetches and re-parses the entire feed every hour; deleting the method and the require removes the false signal and the only use of digest/sha1 in the file.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `require 'digest/sha1'` exists solely for `feed_key`, but `feed_key` is never called anywhere in the diff (and no other conditional-fetch logic using that key is present). As written, `poll_feed` always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` on each run, so the `feed-modified:<sha1>` key suggests throttling/caching that is not actually implemented. Removing `feed_key` and the digest require would avoid misleading future maintainers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] import_remote — the open(url) fetch plus ruby-readability extraction with the tags/attributes whitelist that serves on-demand embedding, TopicRetriever's fetch_http fallback, and the disqus importer — is exercised by no test in the diff. A regression in the readability integration (whitelist option handling, title/content extraction, encoding failures) breaks the primary content-import path only at runtime inside background jobs, invisible to CI and to operators until embeds silently stay stuck on the loading page.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (uses `open(url).read` + `Readability::Document.new(..., tags:, attributes:)`) and wires it into two primary flows: `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` (`TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, @embed_url)`) and the Disqus importer (`TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`). The added specs cover `TopicEmbed.import` and high-level `TopicRetriever#retrieve` call gating, but there is no test exercising `import_remote` itself (no stubbing of `open`, no assertions about Readability title/content extraction, whitelist behavior, or encoding/parse failures). This is a specific, diff-grounded test gap for newly added nontrivial integration logic rather than a direct functional defect proven in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The import task removes the documented `-c/--category` method_option and all category wiring with no deprecation note, changing the task's public CLI surface. Operators running existing `thor disqus:import -c <category>` commands break: the value is no longer a known option so it is passed as a positional argument to a task that takes none and the invocation errors, and there is no longer any way to direct imports into a chosen category instead of Uncategorized.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly removes the public CLI option and its behavior: `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` is deleted from `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, along with all wiring that read `options[:category]` and passed `category: category_id` into `PostCreator`. The import now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])` with no category support. This means existing operator invocations like `thor disqus:import -c <category>` will fail due to an unknown option, and there is no longer any mechanism in this task to target a category, changing/breaking documented behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new raw_html cook path returns raw HTML with no sanitization step anywhere in the import pipeline, silently dropping the 'untrusted HTML must be sanitized' requirement. Any markup in polled RSS/Atom item content (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 passes CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content) straight to TopicEmbed.import — over plain-HTTP fetches that are MITM-able and commonly carry comment/guest text), any readability-scraped attribute like href='javascript:…' (topic_embed.rb:48-50 whitelists tags but never filters URL schemes), and the embed_url interpolated raw into the imported_from footer at topic_embed.rb:13 (a quote in the URL breaks out of the single-quoted href) are all stored verbatim as post.cooked and rendered with `raw post.cooked` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19 and on the forum topic page — stored XSS in the forum origin for every visitor.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a `:raw_html` cook mode that explicitly bypasses the normal cooking/rendering pipeline: `Post#cook` returns `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/post.rb). `TopicEmbed.import` sets this mode for imported posts (`PostCreator.new(... cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])`) and passes HTML content through largely unchanged (topic_embed.rb), while `embed/best.html.erb` renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19). There is no sanitization shown in the import path (poll_feed.rb passes RSS `content` through; import_remote.rb whitelists tags/attrs but does not validate URL schemes), and the footer interpolates `url` into a single-quoted href without escaping (`<a href='#{url}'>...`), allowing quote-breaking. Together, this is a verifiable stored-XSS risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] poll_feed reads i.content on every feed item with no presence check or per-item error handling, so the first item without a content element aborts the entire feed poll. For an RSS 2.0 feed whose items carry only <description> (no content:encoded) or an Atom feed using <summary>, i.content is nil and nil.scrub raises NoMethodError mid-loop; with sidekiq_options retry: false the job dies at that item on every hourly run, so no items after it are ever imported and feed polling is permanently stalled — and spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb only stubs the flag gating, never the loop body, so nothing detects it.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the loop unconditionally does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If a feed item lacks a `content` field (common for RSS 2.0 items that only have `<description>` or Atom `<summary>`), `i.content` can be `nil`, and `nil.scrub` will raise `NoMethodError`, aborting the entire job mid-loop. There is no per-item rescue, and `sidekiq_options retry: false` means it will keep failing on the same item each run, preventing later items from importing. The spec `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` only tests gating and never exercises the loop body, so it wouldn’t catch this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] topic_id_for_embed and TopicEmbed.import match embed URLs by exact string with no canonicalization, so the same article reached via two spellings of its URL creates two topics. When the RSS item link and the discourseEmbedUrl the site owner configures differ by scheme (http vs https), trailing slash, or query string (utm params, ?p=123 style permalinks — all common), the lookup misses, the controller enqueues RetrieveTopic again, and a second TopicEmbed plus second topic is created for the same article, permanently splitting the discussion across duplicates.

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, TopicEmbed lookups are strict string matches on `embed_url` with no normalization: `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` does `where(embed_url: embed_url)` and `TopicEmbed.import` does `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first`, with a unique DB index only on the raw string. The controller (`EmbedController#best`) and retriever (`TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`) also check existence using the exact `@embed_url`. Since embed URLs can legitimately vary by scheme, trailing slash, or tracking/query params, the same article can be treated as different `embed_url` values and result in multiple TopicEmbeds/topics for one article (discussion split).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] TopicEmbed has no lifecycle handling: nothing in the diff removes the row when its topic or post is deleted, and the update path dereferences embed.post with no nil guard. After a moderator deletes an imported topic (posts cascade, the topic_embeds row survives), every embed/best request for that article calls TopicView.new on a nonexistent topic_id and 500s inside the site's comment box forever; and when that article's content next changes, the hourly PollFeed hits embed.post == nil and PostRevisor.new(nil) raises NoMethodError on nil.raw, killing the whole feed job every run.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `TopicEmbed` rows that are not tied to lifecycle cleanup: `TopicEmbed` only has `belongs_to :topic` / `:post` with no `dependent:` behavior, and the migration adds no FK constraints, so deleting the associated topic/post can leave an orphaned `topic_embeds` row. The update path in `TopicEmbed.import` does `post = embed.post` and then unconditionally `PostRevisor.new(post)` when the SHA changes, which will raise if `embed.post` is nil. Similarly, `EmbedController#best` uses `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` (pluck of `topic_id`) and then `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)` without verifying the topic still exists. These are concrete nil/invalid-reference failure modes grounded in the added code paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] ensure_embeddable hard-fails on any request whose browser sends no Referer, with no fallback validation of the embed request. Visitors using privacy extensions, corporate proxies that strip Referer, or referrer-policy-suppressing setups get Discourse::InvalidAccess (a 403 error page) rendered inside the comment box on every view of every embedded article, with no way for the site owner to serve them; this client population is entirely unaddressed.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, access is denied unless `URI(request.referer || '').host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. When `request.referer` is nil/blank (e.g., Referrer stripped or `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`), `URI('')` yields a nil host, which fails the equality check and raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess` ('invalid referer host'), rendering an error instead of the embed. The spec explicitly asserts this behavior (`it "raises an error with no referer"`). There is no alternative validation path using `params[:embed_url]` or similar fallback in this controller, so this client population cannot be served.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] absolutize_urls treats protocol-relative URLs (//host/path) as root-relative and rewrites them into broken host-prefixed paths. href/src values in the era-standard protocol-relative form ('//cdn.example.com/img.png' — start_with?('/') matches and sub(/^\/+/, '') strips both slashes) become 'http://blog.com/cdn.example.com/img.png', so any feed or scraped article using protocol-relative links renders with permanently broken images and links in the embedded topic.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls, both link and image rewriting use `if href.present? && href.start_with?('/')` (and similarly for `src`) and then set `"#{prefix}/#{href.sub(/^\/+/, '')}"`. Protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/img.png` satisfy `start_with?('/')`, and `sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both slashes, producing `cdn.example.com/img.png`, which then becomes `http://<original-host>/cdn.example.com/img.png`—a broken URL. The finding matches this exact behavior in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The only spec for the found-topic path mocks TopicView to return nil and no spec renders any embed view, so the feature's core acceptance criterion — which posts the embed actually shows — is never verified. The suite passes with @topic_view set to the mock's nil (best.html.erb:2 would NoMethodError on nil.posts if views rendered, and render_views is off), so TopicView's real handling of the {best: 5} option, the post selection, and the entire rendered output ship untested; a regression in any of them is invisible to CI.

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`, the “topic_id is found” example sets `TopicView.expects(:new).with(123, nil, {best: 5})` but does not stub a return value, so Mocha will return `nil` by default. The controller assigns `@topic_view = TopicView.new(...)` and would then render `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`, whose first conditional calls `@topic_view.posts.present?`—this would raise `NoMethodError` if views were rendered. Controller specs don’t render views by default (no `render_views` here), and there are no other specs rendering `embed/best` or `embed/loading`, so the embed page output and TopicView’s real behavior with `{best: 5}` are not actually exercised by CI.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The spec titled 'is 404 without an embed_url' asserts only response.should_not be_success, never the 404 status it promises. params.require(:embed_url) actually raises ActionController::ParameterMissing (surfacing as a 400/500, not a 404) and the assertion passes anyway, so the named acceptance criterion is unverified and any error status — including a 500 — is accepted as green.

adjudication.rationale: In spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb, the example named "is 404 without an embed_url" only asserts `response.should_not be_success` after `get :best` with no params. In EmbedController#best, `params.require(:embed_url)` will raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing`, so the request will fail, but the spec does not assert a 404 (or any specific status) and would pass for other failure statuses (e.g., 400/500). This is a concrete, diff-grounded test weakness/mismatch between the spec title and what it verifies, not a runtime defect introduced by the controller itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The loading view reloads every 30 seconds unconditionally and the retrieval pipeline has no terminal failure state or retry budget. When import permanently fails (source article 404s, embed_by_username user is missing, content is unparseable), every visitor's browser reloads the iframe twice a minute forever — continuous request load from every embedded page, no user-visible failure message, and no operator signal that anything is broken.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a loading iframe page that unconditionally reloads every 30s (`app/views/embed/loading.html.erb` calls `document.location.reload()` in a `setTimeout`). `EmbedController#best` renders this loading view whenever no existing `TopicEmbed` exists (it enqueues `:retrieve_topic` and renders `loading`). The retrieval path has clear permanent-failure outcomes with no UI fallback: e.g., `TopicRetriever#retrieve` will skip `perform_retrieve` if `invalid_host?` is true (embed_url host != `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`), and `fetch_http` returns without creating an embed if the posting user can't be found (`return if user.blank?`). In these cases, the embed will never be created, so the iframe stays on the loading page and will reload indefinitely, generating ongoing request load with no terminal error state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] embeddable_host is stored as free text with no validation or normalization while every code path compares it to the exact downcased URI host. An admin who enters 'http://myblog.com', 'myblog.com/', or a capitalized host makes every embed request fail the referer check with a 403 and no diagnostic anywhere — all embeds silently never work and nothing in the UI or logs explains why.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (config/site_settings.yml) and enforces exact string equality against `URI(...).host` in both `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` (`URI(request.referer||'').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`) and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` (`SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host`). There is no normalization/validation of the setting value in this diff, so admin inputs like including a scheme (`http://...`) or a trailing slash would not match `.host` and would break embedding. However, the finding overstates details: the code does not "downcase" the URI host anywhere, and failures are not totally silent because `ensure_embeddable` raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess` with messages like 'invalid referer host'. This is still a concrete, diff-grounded robustness/config UX issue but not an inherent logic/security defect for correctly-configured values.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] feed_key is defined and never called — dead code left over from a dropped skip-unchanged-feed requirement. The intended conditional-fetch check was silently dropped, so every hourly run (and every retrieve-triggered run inside TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve) re-parses the entire feed and re-processes every item, and the next reader must reverse-engineer whether feed_key was supposed to gate something.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `feed_key` is defined but never referenced anywhere in the diff. The `poll_feed` method always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates `rss.items.each`, with no conditional GET / modified-since/etag gating, so each scheduled run re-parses the full feed and attempts to import every item. Additionally, `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` when `feed_polling_enabled?`, which can trigger the same full-feed parse during embed retrieval. This is a real, diff-grounded maintainability/performance concern and dead-code issue, but not a clear correctness defect because `TopicEmbed.import` de-duplicates by `embed_url` and only updates when `content_sha1` changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The migration creates topic_embeds with force: true, and the PR also retrofits force: true into the already-shipped create_top_topics migration. In any environment where the table already holds rows when this migration runs (restored backup, re-baselined schema_migrations), create_table force silently drops all embed data; and editing the shipped top_topics migration means already-deployed databases never receive the change while fresh ones do, diverging environments.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true` in the new migration (db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb) and also retrofits `force: true` into an existing migration (db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb). `force: true` will drop/recreate the table if it already exists, and modifying an already-shipped migration is a maintenance/deployment concern. However, the finding’s concrete data-loss scenario (table already populated when the migration runs) and “diverging environments” outcome are speculative from the diff alone since migrations normally run once and the schema outcome for `top_topics` is unchanged on fresh installs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The header conditional is closed with `<%- end if %>`, which only parses because ERB makes the next emitted text append the modifier's condition (an always-truthy buffer-append guard). The next person to edit this template — inserting a code-only tag, or removing the following blank line and text — changes the guard's condition or breaks the file's Ruby at compile time, turning every embed/best render into a 500; no reader can tell this line is load-bearing on what follows it.

adjudication.rationale: In app/views/embed/best.html.erb the header conditional ends with `<%- end if %>` instead of `<%- end %>`. As written, this is not a clean/intentional Ruby construct and in an ERB template can end up depending on the next emitted ERB buffer append (plain text / `<%=` output) to satisfy the postfix `if` condition, making the template fragile and hard to safely edit. It’s a real, diff-grounded landmine, but the diff itself doesn’t show a current failing render (it likely still compiles/works today), so it’s better classified as a maintainability/correctness risk rather than a demonstrated bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] PostRevisor accepts new raw but never touches cook_method, so staff edits to imported raw_html posts are saved without ever being cooked. A moderator who edits an imported article through the standard editor gets their markdown rendered verbatim as source text (Post#cook returns raw unchanged for raw_html posts), visibly breaking the post after a routine moderation action with no UI path to fix it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `Post.cook_method` with a `:raw_html` mode where `Post#cook` returns `raw` and skips the cooking pipeline (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`). Imported posts are created with `cook_method: :raw_html` (TopicEmbed.import -> PostCreator opts). However, `PostRevisor#revise!`/`update_post` only updates `@post.raw` and saves, and never updates `cook_method` based on the new content. So if an imported `raw_html` post is later edited through the normal revise path (which supplies new_raw), it will remain `:raw_html` and will continue to bypass cooking, causing non-HTML edits (e.g., markdown) to display verbatim.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The raw_html early return skips Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook), silently making a public plugin API conditional on cook_method. Any plugin registering an after_post_cook filter (transforms, sanitizers) never runs on imported posts — exactly the posts most likely to carry untrusted HTML — so plugin users get silent behavior divergence with no error or warning.

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/post.rb, Post#cook now returns `raw` early when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which bypasses `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)` entirely. The diff also introduces imported posts that explicitly set `cook_method: :raw_html` (TopicEmbed.import uses PostCreator with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`). Therefore any plugin relying on the `:after_post_cook` hook will not run for these imported posts, creating silent behavior divergence; and because these posts contain externally sourced HTML, skipping post-cook filters/sanitizers is a potentially serious security/correctness issue grounded in the code shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Every best request for an unknown embed_url enqueues a RetrieveTopic job with no enqueue-side dedup; the 60-second throttle lives only inside the job. A popular article whose import keeps failing (or before the first job runs) enqueues one Sidekiq job per page view, flooding the queue with no-op jobs that each still hit Redis and the database.

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url) is nil it unconditionally calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ... embed_url: embed_url) on every request and renders 'loading'. There is no enqueue-side deduplication or throttle in the controller/job enqueue path. The only 60s throttle is inside TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently? (called during the job’s execution), so many identical Sidekiq jobs can still be queued before any runs or if retrieval repeatedly fails.
