adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] An embed's identity is exact string equality on embed_url with no canonicalization on either producer path: the RSS poll stores the feed's item link (commonly carrying utm query params, feedburner redirect hosts, or a trailing slash that differ from the live page URL) while the retrieve path stores whatever discourseEmbedUrl string the blog template supplies. The same article gets two topics: the scheduled poll imports the feed-link variant, then the first pageview's lookup misses, the retrieve job re-runs the poll (still missing, since the stored key differs by a query string or slash), and fetch_http creates a second topic under the page URL — discussion splits between two topics and the feed keeps updating the twin that no visitor ever sees.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows TopicEmbed lookup/uniqueness is based on exact `embed_url` string equality with no normalization: `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` in `TopicEmbed.import`, `topic_id_for_embed` does `where(embed_url: embed_url)`, and `TopicRetriever` checks `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?`. The RSS path (`Jobs::PollFeed`) stores `i.link` (or `i.id`) as-is, while the embed pageview path supplies `params[:embed_url]` from `discourseEmbedUrl` and later `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, @embed_url)` stores that as-is. If these differ only by query params/trailing slash/redirect host, the existence checks will miss and `TopicEmbed.import` will create a second topic (unique index won’t prevent it because the strings differ), splitting discussion as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] absolutize_urls only rewrites href/src values starting with '/' and uses `href.sub(/^\/+/, '')`, which strips BOTH leading slashes of protocol-relative URLs, mangling `//cdn.example.com/img.png` into `http://blog.example.com/cdn.example.com/img.png` (while bare relative paths like `img/foo.png` are left unabsolutized entirely). Imported articles using protocol-relative asset URLs — the standard pattern for CDN images and links in feeds — render broken images and dead links inside the embedded post, and the corrupted absolute URLs are persisted into the topic's raw and cooked.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, the rewrite condition is `href.start_with?('/')` / `src.start_with?('/')` and it replaces with `"#{prefix}/#{href.sub(/^\/+/, '')}"` (same for `src`). This will also match protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/img.png` and `sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both leading slashes, producing `cdn.example.com/img.png`, which then becomes `http://<embed_host>/cdn.example.com/img.png`—a corrupted URL. Additionally, bare relative paths like `img/foo.png` are not rewritten at all. This is verifiable from the diff and would break imported content using standard protocol-relative assets.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] retrieved_recently? writes the 60-second throttle with two separate redis calls (`$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by `$redis.expire`) instead of an atomic SET-with-TTL, so a worker kill or connection drop between the two leaves `retrieved:<url>` with no expiry. That embed_url is then throttled forever — every subsequent retrieve_topic job returns at the throttle check, the page is never fetched or imported, and the blog shows the 'Loading Discussion' reload loop indefinitely with nothing indicating that a stale redis key is the cause.

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/topic_retriever.rb` the throttle uses two separate Redis operations: `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the worker crashes or the connection drops after `setnx` but before `expire`, the key `retrieved:<embed_url>` can be left without a TTL. Since `retrieved_recently?` returns `true` when the key already exists, that URL would be throttled indefinitely, preventing `perform_retrieve` from running and leaving the embed in the "loading" state permanently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] embeddable_host is a free-text site setting compared against the bare host extracted by URI(...).host in both ensure_embeddable and TopicRetriever#invalid_host?, with no normalization or validation of the stored value anywhere. An operator who enters 'http://blog.example.com' or 'blog.example.com/' (the natural way to fill a field described only as a host) permanently fails the referer check on every embed request and invalid_host? on every retrieve — every iframe errors and no embed ever imports, with no message indicating the value's format is the cause.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (free-text in `config/site_settings.yml`) and then compares it as a raw string against `URI(...).host` in both `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` (`URI(request.referer||'').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`) and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` (`SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host`). The diff shows no normalization/validation of the setting value, so values like `http://blog.example.com` or `blog.example.com/` would indeed never match the bare host and would break embedding/retrieval. However, this is a robustness/UX/config-validation gap rather than an inherent functional bug when configured as intended (a plain host string).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] fetch_http silently returns when embed_by_username is blank or names a nonexistent user, and the entire retrieve path (controller enqueue → job → retriever → import) emits no log line or error anywhere, while EmbedController's guard validates embeddable_host but never embed_by_username. A missing or mistyped embed_by_username produces a completely silent failure: every blog pageview enqueues a job that no-ops, the loading template reloads every 30 seconds forever, and the operator has no diagnostic to distinguish misconfiguration from slowness.

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` does `User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first` and then `return if user.blank?` (lib/topic_retriever.rb), so when `embed_by_username` is left at its default `''` or points to a nonexistent user, retrieval silently no-ops with no logging/error. `EmbedController#best` enqueues `:retrieve_topic` and renders `loading` when no embed exists (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb), and the loading view reloads every 30s (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb), producing an indefinite loading loop with no diagnostic. `ensure_embeddable` validates only `embeddable_host`/referer and does not validate `embed_by_username`, so the misconfiguration is not caught early.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] feed_key builds a `feed-modified:<sha1>` redis cache key that no code in this diff ever reads or writes, indicating an unfinished conditional-fetch optimization that was never wired in. Readers assume feed caching exists when every hourly run actually re-fetches and re-processes the entire feed (one TopicEmbed SELECT per item, plus a full HTTP fetch); as shipped it is dead code that misdocuments behavior — delete the method or wire it up.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `feed_key` constructs a Redis key (`"feed-modified:<sha1>"`) but nothing in this diff calls `feed_key` or uses that key to read/write Redis. The polling logic always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates all items each run, so the method is dead/unfinished optimization rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The rewritten Disqus import replaces `PostCreator.new(..., created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), category: category_id)` with `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, whose opts only forwards :title and whose TopicEmbed.import path never accepts or forwards created_at. Every Disqus thread re-imported with this task is timestamped 'now' — the chronological order of the migrated forum is destroyed (all topics sort as brand-new and original posting dates are unrecoverable), and the previously supported :category option was dropped with no replacement.

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the Disqus thread creation switched from `PostCreator.new(..., created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), category: category_id)` to `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` only uses `opts[:title]` (and otherwise `doc.title`) and calls `TopicEmbed.import`, which constructs `PostCreator.new(... title:, raw:, skip_validations:, cook_method:)` without any `created_at` (or category) forwarding. Therefore imported topics/posts will get default timestamps ("now") and the previously supported `--category` option was removed with no replacement, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The update branch revises only the post's raw body (PostRevisor#revise! receives new_raw and nothing else) and never revises the topic's title, so a retitle in the feed propagates the content change but not the headline. A blog that renames an article keeps a Discourse topic whose title and URL slug reflect the old headline forever — the change-tracking design (content_sha1) detects that the article changed but applies only half the change, so the embedded discussion diverges from the source it mirrors.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path (when an existing `TopicEmbed` is found) only revises the post body via `PostRevisor#revise!(user, absolutize_urls(url, contents), ...)` and never updates the topic/post title. Additionally, `content_sha1` is computed from `contents` only (`Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(contents)`), so a feed title change with unchanged content will not trigger any update at all. This means retitles in the source feed will not propagate and the Discourse topic title/slug can remain stale indefinitely.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Line 6 closes the header conditional with `<%- end if %>`, which compiles to the Ruby fragment `end if` with no condition expression and therefore fails ERB template compilation with a syntax error. Every /embed/best request that finds a topic raises ActionView::Template::Error when the template is compiled, so after loading.html.erb's 30-second reload swaps in the populated view the embed iframe serves an error page on every embedding site — the feature never renders comments; the new embed_controller_spec never renders views (no render_views), so CI stays green while the shipped artifact is dead.
matched_golden_ids: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same core problem: the ERB/Ruby block is closed with `end if`, which is invalid syntax in this context and causes a template compilation/render error; it should be closed with just `end`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Post#cook returns raw completely unsanitized when cook_method is raw_html, bypassing the Discourse cooking/sanitization pipeline that every other post must pass through — the platform's core accepted security constraint. HTML fetched from the embedded host is stored and served as live markup: poll_feed passes i.content straight through with only CGI.unescapeHTML (which also re-materializes escaped entities into active tags) and no tag/attribute filtering, so a script/iframe/onerror payload in the feed content executes on the Discourse origin in every viewer's session — including staff — in both the topic page and the `raw post.cooked` embed view.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds `Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw` when `cook_method` is `raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline (`post_analyzer.cook` + plugin filters). New feed import paths set this mode: `TopicEmbed.import` calls `PostCreator.new(..., raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents), ..., cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])`. In `Jobs::PollFeed`, `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` is passed into `TopicEmbed.import` with no sanitization/tag filtering, and the embed view renders it via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. Since `post.cooked == post.raw` for `raw_html` (confirmed by the new spec expectation), malicious HTML from the feed can be stored and rendered as live markup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The imported-from footer interpolates url into single-quoted HTML with only a `^https?://` regex guard, so a quote in the URL path escapes the href attribute (HTML5 tokenization starts a new attribute even without whitespace). An attacker who can place a link on the embedding host (e.g. a blog comment linking to /embed/best?embed_url=http://host/?s='onclick='...) supplies a referer that passes the embeddable_host check and an embed_url whose host passes TopicRetriever's host check while its query string carries the payload; the resulting raw_html post stores the injected event-handler attribute and executes on the Discourse origin when the topic is viewed.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code appends an "imported from" footer using `"#{url}"` and then stores it as `raw_html` (`PostCreator.new(... cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])`), and the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. The only validation on `url` is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent quotes or other HTML-breaking characters in the URL. Therefore a crafted URL containing a single quote can break out of the `href='...'` attribute and inject additional attributes/JS, leading to XSS on Discourse origin when the cooked/raw HTML is displayed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The Disqus import task deletes the documented `--category`/`-c` option and the category lookup, so imported threads can no longer be targeted at a category. Operators running the previously-accepted `disqus:import --category X` invocation either hit an unknown-option failure or have the flag silently ignored, landing every imported thread in Uncategorized with no replacement path anywhere in this diff.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor the PR explicitly removes `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` and deletes the subsequent `category_id` lookup and passing `category: category_id` into `PostCreator`. The replacement call `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])` has no category argument/path shown in this diff. Therefore, the previously supported `disqus:import --category/-c` CLI option will now be rejected as an unknown option (Thor) and there is no diff-shown replacement to target a category, matching the finding’s claim of broken operator behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The rewritten import replaces PostCreator.new(..., created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), category: category_id) with TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title]), dropping the original thread timestamp for the first post. Imported OP posts carry the import-run timestamp while the unchanged reply loop keeps original Disqus dates, producing topics whose first post is dated after its replies and destroying the chronological fidelity the importer existed to preserve; the post body also changes from a permalink pointer to a full remote-page scrape with no acceptance of that content change.

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the OP creation changed from `PostCreator.new(..., created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]) ...)` to `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` -> `TopicEmbed.import` creates the post via `PostCreator.new(user, title: ..., raw: ..., skip_validations: true, cook_method: ...)` without passing `created_at`, so the first post will get the current time rather than the Disqus thread timestamp. This is a verifiable loss of imported timestamp fidelity introduced by the diff. The post body content also clearly changes from a permalink stub to a scraped remote page (`ruby-readability`), which is an intentional behavior change but not required to validate the timestamp bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] TopicEmbed declares belongs_to :topic and belongs_to :post with no dependent-destroy, callback, or cleanup path anywhere in this diff, so deleting an imported topic leaves the TopicEmbed row dangling. Staff deleting an imported topic (normal moderation) permanently breaks that URL's embed — topic_id_for_embed returns the dead topic_id and TopicView.new raises in the widget forever — and the next feed update whose content changed calls PostRevisor.new(embed.post) on nil, raising NoMethodError inside the hourly poll (sidekiq retry: false) and wedging feed import at that item while later items never import.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `TopicEmbed` with `belongs_to :topic` / `:post` and a table (`topic_embeds`) that has only a unique index on `embed_url`—no FK/cascade and no `dependent: :destroy`/cleanup logic shown. `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` will keep returning a `topic_id` even if the topic/post is deleted, and `TopicEmbed.import`’s update path does `post = embed.post` then `PostRevisor.new(post)` with no nil-guard, which will raise if the referenced post has been deleted (AR association returns nil when the row is gone). This is a real correctness hole introduced/exposed by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] poll_feed calls `i.content.scrub`, but String#scrub exists only in Ruby 2.1.0+ (released 2013-12-25, after this branch) while this Discouse-era runtime is Ruby 2.0.0, and i.content is nil for feed items without a content element. On the deployed Ruby the very first feed item raises NoMethodError and the hourly job dies with retry: false before importing anything, so the RSS import feature ships non-functional; no test in the diff executes poll_feed's body (the specs stub it out), so the crash is invisible to CI.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the job unconditionally does `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If a feed item lacks a `content` element (common in RSS; sometimes only `description` exists), `i.content` can be `nil`, making `nil.scrub` raise `NoMethodError`, which would abort the hourly job (and it is configured `sidekiq_options retry: false`). The claim about Ruby 2.0 vs 2.1 for `String#scrub` isn’t verifiable from the diff, but the nil-safety issue is directly grounded in the added code and can break the feature at runtime.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve synchronously executes the entire hourly feed poll (Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})) inside a per-embed background job on every new embed URL. Each first-time visitor to any page of the embedding site spawns a full feed parse plus a remote fetch and topic import per feed item, turning a 60-second-throttled single-URL widget request into a heavy sidekiq job that congests the queue on blogs with large feeds, and the widget's success silently depends on the feed settings being configured even though fetching the single URL would suffice.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` does a synchronous full feed poll when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true: `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` (lib/topic_retriever.rb). This method is invoked from the per-URL background job `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` (app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb) which is enqueued on first-time embed requests (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). As written, each new embed URL can trigger a feed parse/import of *all* items before falling back to `fetch_http`, which is a significant performance/queue-architecture concern rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] PollFeed#feed_key computes a feed-modified cache key that nothing in this diff ever reads or writes — the conditional-poll throttle it was written for was abandoned mid-design. The only mechanism that could have throttled the retriever's inline full-feed polls (topic_retriever.rb:41) does not exist, leaving those polls unthrottled, and maintainers reading the method believe modification-based polling is wired; deleting the method changes no behavior.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `feed_key` computes `"feed-modified:#{Digest::SHA1...}"` but nothing in this diff ever uses it (no reads/writes to Redis/cache keyed by it), so deleting it would not change behavior. Also, `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` when `feed_polling_enabled?` is true, and the only throttle shown (`retrieved_recently?`) is per-`@embed_url` (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), not per feed URL, so different embed URLs can still trigger repeated full-feed polls. This is a real, diff-grounded design/maintenance issue, though not a correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] fetch_http returns silently when embed_by_username does not resolve to a user (`return if user.blank?`), and poll_feed:28 does the same, with no log entry, no error, and no admin-time validation that pairs the settings. An admin who sets embeddable_host but not embed_by_username gets a widget that renders 'Loading Discussion...' and reloads every 30 seconds forever while the job chain completes 'successfully' — nothing anywhere indicates which setting is missing, so the misconfiguration is undiagnosable from either the blog or the Discourse logs.

adjudication.rationale: Verified in diff: when an embed doesn’t exist, `EmbedController#best` enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` and renders `embed/loading` (which reloads every 30s). In the retrieval path, `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` does `user = User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first` and then `return if user.blank?` with no logging or error. Since `embed_by_username` defaults to `''` in `config/site_settings.yml`, a typical “not set” state leads to querying `username_lower: ''`, `user.blank?` => true, and the job exits successfully but creates no `TopicEmbed`, so the iframe stays on “Loading Discussion...” forever. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` has the same silent `return if user.blank?` behavior. This makes the system appear to hang under common misconfiguration, matching the finding’s core claim.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] /embed/best accepts anonymous GETs and unconditionally enqueues RetrieveTopic, with throttling keyed only per embed_url (the redis key retrieved:<url>), not per client or IP. An attacker iterates embed_url=http://host/<random-path> — each unique path passes the embeddable_host check and defeats the per-URL 60-second throttle — to enqueue unbounded jobs that each create a junk topic under embed_by_username with skip_validations, flooding the sidekiq queue and the site's topic lists with scraped garbage from a plain curl loop.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a public `get 'embed/best' => 'embed#best'` endpoint. In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil it unconditionally enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: current_user.try(:id), embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading`, with no auth requirement shown. The only gate is `ensure_embeddable`, which checks `request.referer` host against `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`—a header an attacker can spoof. The job’s throttling in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` is keyed solely by the full embed URL string (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), so varying the path/query on the same allowed host bypasses the 60s throttle. `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which fetches and imports remote content and `TopicEmbed.import` creates a topic/post via `PostCreator` with `skip_validations: true` and `cook_method: :raw_html`, enabling queue flooding and potentially大量 junk topics/posts under `embed_by_username`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The raw_html early-return in Post#cook returns before Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...), silently ending the platform contract that every cooked post passes through the plugin filter. Installs running plugins hooked into after_post_cook (image URL rewriters, lazy-loading, analytics transforms) get imported posts where those transforms never ran — inconsistently rendered in both the embed iframe and topic pages — with no opt-in for plugin authors, who will debug phantom 'sometimes my filter doesn't fire' behavior.

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/post.rb, Post#cook now immediately `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which bypasses `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)` that previously wrapped all cooked output. This is a real, diff-grounded behavioral change that can break/skip plugin transformations for posts created with `cook_method: :raw_html` (e.g., TopicEmbed.import via PostCreator). However, the diff also explicitly states the intent is to “skip the rendering pipeline” for certain imported posts, and the PR doesn’t establish a hard “must always run” contract for plugin authors, so it’s more of an API/compatibility/architecture concern than a provable correctness bug in core.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The embed PR silently modifies the previously-committed, unrelated CreateTopTopics migration to add `force: true`, changing create_table from fail-on-collision to drop-and-recreate. Any database where top_topics already exists without this version recorded (schemas created from a sibling branch's variant of this migration) silently loses its top_topics rows when the migration runs, and a change to an accepted migration's semantics landed inside a PR titled for embed URL handling with no review of migration behavior.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does modify an existing, unrelated migration: `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` changes `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists and recreate it, which can cause silent data loss in environments where `top_topics` exists but this migration is still pending or its version isn’t recorded. This is a real, diff-grounded behavioral change with data-loss implications and is unrelated to the embedding feature changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] TopicEmbed.import stores external content in posts with cook_method raw_html (line 22) and interpolates the feed-supplied url unescaped into the "<a href='#{url}'>" footer (line 13), so imported markup is rendered verbatim with none of Discourse's HTML sanitization — the Readability path's whitelist (lines 48-49) at most filters tag/attribute names and never URL schemes, so javascript:/data: hrefs survive, while the RSS path applies no content filter at all. Stored XSS on the Discourse origin: hostile RSS item bodies are stored as live script-bearing HTML, and a javascript: link planted on any embeddable-host page (e.g. a blog comment, which Readability keeps because a/href are whitelisted) executes attacker JS in the forum session of every user who opens the imported topic — session/token theft sitewide including staff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces a `cook_method` enum with `:raw_html` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and sets `raw` to `absolutize_urls(url, contents)` where `contents` comes from external RSS bodies (`Jobs::PollFeed` uses `i.content` with only `CGI.unescapeHTML`/`scrub`) or from Readability (`doc.content`). Neither path sanitizes HTML, and the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. Additionally, `TopicEmbed.import` appends a footer containing `#{url}` with only a prefix regex check (`/^https?\:\/\//`), so a malicious URL containing a single quote can inject attributes/markup. Together, this is a verifiable stored XSS risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Post#cook short-circuits with 'return raw' when cook_method is raw_html, placing the return ahead of both post_analyzer.cook (the markdown + Sanitize pipeline that neutralizes script/javascript: URLs in every other post) and Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...), so raw_html posts are stored and served as verbatim HTML. The unsanitized external HTML this same PR imports (TopicEmbed.import) reaches <%= raw post.cooked %> at app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19 and the main topic renderer as executable markup, turning the import feature into a stored-XSS pipeline; plugins registering after_post_cook filters are silently bypassed too.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds Post.cook_methods with :raw_html and changes Post#cook to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which bypasses both `post_analyzer.cook(*args)` (the normal markdown/sanitization pipeline) and `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)` (lib/app/models/post.rb). The same PR imports external HTML into posts via TopicEmbed.import/import_remote without any sanitization shown here (RSS `i.content` and Readability `doc.content`), and then renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Jobs::PollFeed passes each RSS item's body straight into TopicEmbed.import after only CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) — no filtering, with the entity-decode re-arming escaped payloads — where it is stored as raw HTML. Anyone who can influence a single feed item — a compromised or aggregating third-party feed source, or an attacker-modified setting value — gets markup stored and rendered unsanitized in every viewer's session in the forum, including admins, on an hourly schedule.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces Jobs::PollFeed, which takes `i.content` from the parsed feed, applies only `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, and passes it to `TopicEmbed.import` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb). `TopicEmbed.import` creates a post via `PostCreator` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true` (app/models/topic_embed.rb), and `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly for `:raw_html` (app/models/post.rb). The embed view renders `raw post.cooked` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb). There is no sanitization/whitelisting on the RSS content path, and `unescapeHTML` can re-enable escaped markup, so a malicious/compromised feed item can inject unsanitized HTML/JS into rendered output on the hourly schedule.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The only access control on the unauthenticated /embed/best route is comparing the client-supplied Referer header's host to SiteSetting.embeddable_host, and Referer is a trivially forgeable client header, so the gate is cosmetic. Any anonymous client can hit the enqueue branch (line 15) at will: each unique embed_url enqueues a RetrieveTopic job whose 60s throttle is keyed per-URL and only checked after dequeue (and removed entirely for staff user_ids via no_throttle), letting an attacker flood the Sidekiq queue and drive the Discourse server to crawl the embeddable host, re-polling the entire RSS feed inline on every job (the feed_key cache is never used).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a public `get 'embed/best'` route and `EmbedController#best` enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` whenever `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil. The only gate in `ensure_embeddable` is `URI(request.referer || '').host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, which relies on the client-supplied `Referer` header and does not validate `params[:embed_url]` itself. An attacker can supply a forged Referer and spam requests with many unique `embed_url` values, causing unthrottled job enqueue. The 60s throttle in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` is per-URL and only applied during job execution, so many unique URLs still flood Sidekiq. Additionally, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true, `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`, which fetches and iterates the entire feed each time; `PollFeed#feed_key` exists but is unused, so there is no caching to prevent repeated full feed polling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] ensure_embeddable sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL — a non-standard value browsers treat as no framing protection — on a page whose only framing restriction is the forgeable Referer check. Any site can frame the embed page (served with the viewer's session cookies) and overlay its 'Continue Discussion' links and content for clickjacking and UI redressing against Discourse users, defeating the SAMEORIGIN protection the rest of the app relies on.
matched_golden_ids: The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same core security issue: setting X-Frame-Options to ALLOWALL effectively removes framing protection and relying on a forgeable Referer check is insufficient, enabling clickjacking/UI redressing. It doesn’t explicitly mention the nil Referer fallback to empty string, but it captures the main vulnerability described in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] invalid_host? compares only URI(...).host — scheme and port are never checked, and the open() at app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 follows HTTP redirects to any host without revalidation — so the embeddable_host allowlist does not constrain what the server actually fetches for an attacker-supplied embed_url. An anonymous embed request for http://<embeddable_host>:8080/x or any redirecting URL on that host (open redirect, shortlink) makes the Discourse server connect to arbitrary ports of that host and fetch attacker-chosen internal hosts, with the response body imported as a publicly readable topic — internal-service content exfiltration.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` which only checks `SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host` (lib/topic_retriever.rb), ignoring scheme and port. When the host matches, it calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, @embed_url)` which does `open(url).read` (app/models/topic_embed.rb) without revalidating the final URL/host after redirects. Since `open-uri` will follow HTTP redirects by default, a URL on the allowed host that redirects elsewhere (or a URL specifying a different port on the same host, e.g. `http://allowed:8080/...`) can cause the server to fetch unintended endpoints while still passing the host-only allowlist check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] PollFeed fetches the admin-set SiteSetting.feed_polling_url with open() and no scheme or host validation, and open-uri follows redirects off-host, so the settings value is an unvalidated server-side fetch target executed on an hourly schedule. A misused or attacker-modified setting (an ftp:// value, or an http feed that 302-redirects to internal addresses) turns the scheduled job into an internal-network fetcher whose output is imported as public forum posts — config must be treated as attacker-controllable input for this sink.
matched_golden_ids: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that PollFeed uses open() on SiteSetting.feed_polling_url without validating scheme/host and notes open-uri redirect behavior, enabling attacker-controlled arbitrary URL fetches (SSRF). This is the same underlying issue as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The postMessage origin gate checks substring containment (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) instead of exact origin equality, so any origin that appears as a substring of the Discourse URL string passes the check. An attacker registering a string-prefix domain twin (e.g. the .co twin of a .com forum URL) can send discourse-resize messages to any page embedding the forum and drive the Discourse iframe's height arbitrarily, enabling UI-redressing on third-party pages.
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same flaw: origin validation uses a substring/indexOf check rather than strict origin equality, allowing attacker-controlled lookalike domains (e.g., evil-discourseUrl.com or similar twins) to bypass the gate.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The layout echoes the fully client-controlled request.referer into a single-quoted inline JavaScript string literal using only ERB HTML-escaping, which leaves single quotes intact, while the only upstream filter (embed_controller.rb:26 URI host check) accepts quote and paren characters in the path because they are RFC2396 mark characters. A request whose Referer is http://<embeddable_host>/');payload// passes the host check and renders the payload outside the string literal in the embed/loading page, executing attacker JS in the Discourse origin for whoever loads the framed embed — reflected XSS via a request header.
matched_golden_ids: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue describes the unescaped/insufficiently escaped request.referer header being embedded into an inline JavaScript string, allowing quote-breaking and reflected XSS. This is the same underlying vulnerability as the golden comment (referer header interpolated into JS without proper escaping leading to XSS).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Each of the three guard specs stubs only one setting of Jobs::PollFeed#execute's three-way && chain and leaves the others at their false defaults from config/site_settings.yml (feed_polling_enabled: false, feed_polling_url: '', embed_by_username: ''), so the unstubbed SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled? short-circuits the conjunction before the condition each test claims to verify is ever evaluated. All three specs stay green even when the guard each one names is deleted from execute: an admin who enables feed polling without setting feed_polling_url gets an hourly job that calls open('') and crashes, and with 'sidekiq_options retry: false' the scheduled job dies silently - the only discriminating example in the file is 'delegates to poll_feed', so the three 'requires' specs provide zero verification of the guards they document.

adjudication.rationale: In `Jobs::PollFeed#execute`, `poll_feed` only runs if `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled? && SiteSetting.feed_polling_url.present? && SiteSetting.embed_by_username.present?` (new code in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`). In `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb`, the three “requires …” examples each stub only one of those settings and leave the others at their defaults from `config/site_settings.yml` (`feed_polling_enabled: false`, `feed_polling_url: ''`, `embed_by_username: ''`). Because the conjunction short-circuits on the other false/blank defaults, those specs don’t actually prove that the specific guard they name is necessary; they would still pass even if that particular check were removed, making them ineffective/misleading tests. However, the diff as written still contains the guards, so this is a test-quality issue rather than a runtime defect introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] 'is 404 without an embed_url' never exercises the missing-parameter path: the before_filter ensure_embeddable runs first and raises on the unstubbed SiteSetting.embeddable_host default '' from config/site_settings.yml, so the observed failure comes from the host guard, params.require(:embed_url) is never reached, and the sole assertion response.should_not be_success passes identically for a 400, a 404, or a 500. Deleting params.require(:embed_url) from EmbedController#best keeps this spec green - the actual missing-embed_url handling is verified by no test in the diff, and the title's claimed 404 status is never asserted, so a regression that turns embed errors into unhandled 500s is indistinguishable from the intended response.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController`, `before_filter :ensure_embeddable` runs before `best` and raises if `SiteSetting.embeddable_host.blank?` (it is configured as `''` in `config/site_settings.yml`). The spec `it "is 404 without an embed_url" do; get :best; response.should_not be_success; end` does not stub `embeddable_host` and therefore will fail due to the host guard in `ensure_embeddable`, never reaching `params.require(:embed_url)` in `best`. Additionally, the test title claims a 404 but asserts only non-success, so it would stay green for various error codes and does not truly verify missing-parameter handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] 'delegates to poll_feed' replaces poll_feed with a mocha expectation, so the item loop inside Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:24-38) - the link/id fallback branch at line 33 and 'content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)' at line 35 - is executed by no test in the diff (checked spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb, the only spec referencing Jobs::PollFeed). A plain RSS 2.0 feed whose items carry description but no content element leaves i.content nil and nil.scrub raises NoMethodError inside the hourly job; with 'retry: false' the failure is silent and importing halts for every subsequent item - a crash a single loop test against a stubbed feed object would have caught.

adjudication.rationale: In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` the code unconditionally does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb). If an RSS item lacks a `content` field (e.g., only has `description`), `i.content` can be `nil`, and `nil.scrub` will raise `NoMethodError`, crashing the scheduled job (with `sidekiq_options retry: false`). The added spec (`spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb`) only asserts `poll_feed` is called and never exercises the item loop, so this crash path is not covered by tests in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] 'Supports updating the post' is the only spec covering TopicEmbed.import's update branch (app/models/topic_embed.rb:31-39) and it passes changed content while asserting only post.cooked =~ /new contents/, leaving the unchanged-content no-revision branch, the embed.update_column(:content_sha1, ...) persistence at line 37, and the replacement of the old body all unasserted (checked spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb). Dropping the update_column call or breaking the sha-equality no-op branch keeps the suite green while the hourly Jobs::PollFeed run re-revises every embedded topic on every poll - silent edit notifications and version churn across all feed content - and a regression that appends rather than replaces the post body also satisfies the =~ assertion.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial update/no-op logic in TopicEmbed.import: it computes content_sha1, and only when it differs (app/models/topic_embed.rb, update branch) it calls PostRevisor#revise! and persists the new sha via embed.update_column(:content_sha1, ...). The only spec exercising the update path (spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb "Supports updating the post") asserts only that `post.cooked` matches `/new contents/`, and does not assert (a) that the post body is replaced rather than appended, (b) that `content_sha1` is updated/persisted, or (c) that the sha-equality branch performs no revision. Therefore the finding correctly identifies a specific test gap where breaking `update_column` or the sha-equality no-op could go undetected, potentially causing repeated revisions during Jobs::PollFeed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Every example in this spec mocks past the real logic - the two valid-host specs stub retrieved_recently? instead of exercising it, and all five stub perform_retrieve - so the 60-second Redis throttle in TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently? (lib/topic_retriever.rb:21-33), the no_throttle staff bypass, and perform_retrieve's dedup/RSS-first/fetch_http paths execute in zero examples (checked spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb and spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb, which replaces TopicRetriever.new with a mock). If the $redis.expire call is dropped, the 'retrieved:<url>' key never expires and embedded articles are throttled forever after their first retrieval - permanently stale embeds in production with no spec failing - and the staff no-throttle contract ships equally unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial throttle/dedup/RSS-first logic in `lib/topic_retriever.rb` (`retrieved_recently?` uses `$redis.setnx` + `$redis.expire`, `no_throttle` bypass, and `perform_retrieve` does dedup + optional RSS poll + `fetch_http`). However, the new specs mostly mock around this logic: `spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb` stubs `retrieved_recently?` in the “valid host” examples and asserts `perform_retrieve` is/ isn’t called rather than exercising Redis behavior; other examples explicitly expect `perform_retrieve` to never run. Additionally, `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` replaces `TopicRetriever.new` with a mock retriever and only asserts `retrieve` is invoked. So the throttle expiry, staff bypass, and `perform_retrieve` paths are not executed by tests in this diff, which is a concrete test coverage gap for newly added behavior (even if the hypothetical '$redis.expire dropped' regression is speculative).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Both success-path specs verify only mock invocations - 'TopicView.expects(:new).with(123, nil, {best: 5})' returns nil and 'retriever.expects(:retrieve)' - and run without render_views, so the rendered output of embed/best (the posts loop, the empty-posts start_discussion branch in app/views/embed/best.html.erb, and app/views/embed/loading.html.erb's reload path) is asserted by nothing in the diff (checked spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb, the only spec touching the endpoint). Template-level regressions - a nil @topic_view dereference, the wrong branch for a topic whose filtered post list is empty, a broken loading reload - reach every production embedding page unverified, because no example in the diff renders either template.

adjudication.rationale: In spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb, the “success” examples only assert collaborator calls (e.g., `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)... retriever.expects(:retrieve)` and `TopicView.expects(:new).with(123, nil, {best: 5})`) and basic response/header checks. The spec does not enable `render_views` and does not assert any rendered content/branching from app/views/embed/best.html.erb or app/views/embed/loading.html.erb (e.g., the posts-present vs. empty branch, the `raw post.cooked` output, or the loading page reload script). This is a concrete, diff-grounded test coverage gap for newly added embedding views/endpoints, not a confirmed runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The only HTTP-level assertions for the success path - response.should be_success and the X-Frame-Options == 'ALLOWALL' security-header check - live in an after hook, hidden from both it blocks and reported as after-hook errors rather than example assertions. A reader of 'tells the topic retriever to work...' sees no assertions at the test site; when a mock expectation fails, the after-hook failure obscures the root cause; and any new test added to this context silently inherits the success-and-header assertions and fails for reasons unrelated to its own claim.

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`, under `context "success"`, the only HTTP-level assertions (`response.should be_success` and `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'].should == "ALLOWALL"`) are placed in an `after do` hook rather than inside each `it` block. This is verifiable in the diff and creates the cited problems: individual examples like "tells the topic retriever..." contain no direct assertions about success/headers, failures may surface as after-hook errors (obscuring the example’s intent), and any newly added example in this context will implicitly inherit these assertions and may fail for reasons unrelated to the example. This is a test structure/maintainability concern rather than a functional defect in production code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The rescue URI::InvalidURIError branch in ensure_embeddable is triggered by no test - spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb covers only a nil referer (lines 24-27) and a matching referer, never a referer string that fails URI() parsing. If the rescue is deleted or misplaced, a request whose Referer header fails URI parsing raises out of the before_filter and 500s every embed hit from that client instead of returning the intended error response - with no spec in the diff failing to reveal it.

adjudication.rationale: In app/controllers/embed_controller.rb, ensure_embeddable compares `URI(request.referer || '').host` and rescues `URI::InvalidURIError` to raise `Discourse::InvalidAccess`. The added controller spec (spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb) covers missing referer and a valid referer, but does not exercise a referer value that is present yet syntactically invalid (triggering the rescue branch). This is a specific missing-test gap for newly introduced nontrivial error-handling logic, not a directly verifiable runtime defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed never runs against real data in the diff's tests - spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb stubs it at both call sites (lines 41 and 49) and spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb never calls it (checked both files), so the read-your-writes contract between the embed_url stored by import and the controller's exact-match lookup (no normalization of trailing slash, scheme, or query) is unverified. If import ever stores a URL differing by a trailing slash or scheme from the string embed.js sends, every embed page finds no topic_id, re-enqueues retrieval on each view, and shows the loading view indefinitely - while the suite stays green because both specs stub the lookup.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `EmbedController#best` relies on `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` doing an exact-match lookup (`TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: embed_url)`), but the controller spec stubs `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` in both relevant examples, so the lookup is never exercised end-to-end against data written by `TopicEmbed.import`. The model spec exercises `import` creation/update behavior but never calls `topic_id_for_embed`, so it doesn’t validate that the stored `embed_url` will be found by the controller with the same string. The concern about URL normalization (trailing slash/scheme/query) is a concrete edge-case risk given the exact-match implementation, but it’s not proven as an actual defect by the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] 'tells the topic retriever to work when no previous embed is found' pins the far end of the chain - a mocked TopicRetriever receiving retrieve - instead of the controller's actual contract at app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 (Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: current_user.try(:id), embed_url: embed_url)), so it passes both for the intended async enqueue and for a naive synchronous TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve inside the request. Dropping user_id from the enqueue payload silently disables the staff no_throttle bypass in Jobs::RetrieveTopic, and converting the endpoint to synchronous retrieval (blocking embed/best on the embedded site's HTTP fetch) both keep CI green, because the mocked retriever receives retrieve either way.

adjudication.rationale: In app/controllers/embed_controller.rb#best, when no topic_id is found it enqueues a background job via `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: current_user.try(:id), embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading`; it does not instantiate `TopicRetriever`. However, spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb's example "tells the topic retriever to work when no previous embed is found" expects `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve` to be called. That pins an implementation detail that isn't in the controller and fails to assert the controller’s actual contract (the enqueue payload, including `user_id` used later by Jobs::RetrieveTopic for `no_throttle`). The finding’s broader point about the spec not guarding the enqueue contract is grounded in the diff, even though some hypothetical scenarios described are not directly verifiable here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] TopicEmbed rows are never cleaned up when their topic or post is destroyed (the diff adds no destroy hook and no admin path to remove an embed), so topic_id_for_embed keeps returning a dead topic_id and the update path dereferences a nil post. After an admin permanently deletes an imported topic, the embed_url maps to the dead topic forever: EmbedController#best sees a non-nil topic_id, builds TopicView on the deleted topic, and the embed iframe errors permanently (the recreate branch never runs), and when the article content next changes PollFeed/RetrieveTopic crash with NoMethodError on nil in PostRevisor.new(embed.post).revise! — with retry:false and no per-item rescue the exception aborts the rss.items loop, so hourly feed importing halts for all subsequent feed items indefinitely.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds TopicEmbed records keyed by embed_url but provides no cleanup when the associated topic/post is deleted (TopicEmbed belongs_to :topic/:post with no dependent behavior, and the migration adds only an index on embed_url). As a result, TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed just plucks a topic_id without validating existence, so EmbedController#best will take the “topic exists” branch and build TopicView on a potentially deleted topic_id, never enqueuing retrieval. Separately, TopicEmbed.import’s update path does `post = embed.post` and then `PostRevisor.new(post)` without guarding against `post` being nil, which would raise if the post was deleted while the TopicEmbed row remains. Jobs::PollFeed has `sidekiq_options retry: false` and no per-item rescue in `rss.items.each`, so such an exception would abort the whole poll run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The Disqus importer now creates topics via TopicEmbed.import_remote, which accepts no created_at (and the -c category option was deleted from the thor task), so the original thread dates previously passed as created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]) are discarded. Every topic imported by 'disqus.thor import' is stamped with the import run's current time instead of its source publish date, destroying the chronological fidelity (latest lists, bump ordering, topic sorting) the prior PostCreator call preserved, and imports can no longer target a category — passing -c now fails as an unknown option and everything lands in uncategorized.

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the importer no longer uses `PostCreator.new(... created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), category: category_id)` and instead calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote`/`.import` create posts via `PostCreator.new(... skip_validations: true, cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])` without passing `created_at` or `category`, so imported topics/posts will be timestamped at import time and cannot be targeted to a category. Additionally, the Thor `:category` option (`-c`) was removed, so `-c` will now be an unknown option.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Adding force: true to the already-committed CreateTopTopics migration makes it silently drop any existing top_topics table (and all its rows) when its up runs against a database that already has the table, instead of failing loudly. On any environment where top_topics exists without this migration recorded as applied (a restore, a re-run, or a teammate's database built from an earlier iteration of the feature), rake db:migrate now silently drops top_topics and all accumulated per-period score rows, wiping the Top pages; previously the same run failed loudly with 'relation top_topics already exists', so this change converts a safe loud failure into silent data loss.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration (db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb) from `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists and recreate it, which can silently delete all rows. This converts the prior loud failure mode (table already exists) into a potentially silent destructive operation if the migration is run in an environment where `top_topics` already exists but this migration is not recorded as applied.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] This diff adds the posts.cook_method column and the topic_embeds table but contains no regeneration of the tracked schema dump (no db/schema.rb or db/structure.sql change appears anywhere in the diff), so the committed schema drifts from the migrations. Environments built from the schema dump instead of running db:migrate (fresh installs via db:schema:load, db:reset, test databases prepared from the committed file) lack cook_method and topic_embeds: Post#cook calls the missing cook_method attribute and raises NoMethodError on every post creation/edit, and every embed request fails with 'relation topic_embeds does not exist'.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new migrations that add `posts.cook_method` (20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb) and a new `topic_embeds` table (20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb), but there is no corresponding update to any committed schema dump file (`db/schema.rb` or `db/structure.sql`) anywhere in the diff. If this project relies on a tracked schema dump for `db:schema:load`/test DB setup, that dump would omit `cook_method` and `topic_embeds`, causing the newly added code paths (e.g., `Post#cook` referencing `cook_method`, `TopicEmbed` queries) to fail on fresh installs/tests built from the dump.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] create_table :topic_embeds uses force: true, so the migration drops any pre-existing topic_embeds table — including its embed_url→topic_id mapping — instead of erroring when re-run. A developer or staging box re-running this migration after a rollback (db:migrate:redo) or carrying the table from an earlier iteration of this branch silently loses every embed mapping; the next PollFeed/TopicRetriever run then finds no TopicEmbed row for each feed item and re-imports the same articles as duplicate topics with duplicated post content.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb` explicitly does `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`, which will drop an existing `topic_embeds` table if present instead of failing. That can cause silent data loss of existing `embed_url` mappings, and subsequent logic (e.g., `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` used in `EmbedController#best` and `TopicRetriever`) will treat embeds as missing and re-import/create new topics, leading to duplication as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false forces a full rewrite of the posts table under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on the PostgreSQL versions this app runs (constant-default ADD COLUMN only became catalog-only in PG 11). On any forum with a large posts table, rake db:migrate during deploy blocks all reads and writes on posts for the full table-rewrite duration — a sitewide outage window proportional to posts size; adding the column nullable, backfilling in batches, and only then constraining bounds the lock to short scans instead of a whole-table rewrite.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a migration `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false` (db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb). On PostgreSQL versions prior to 11, adding a column with a non-null constant default is known to rewrite the whole table and take an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, which can cause a long deploy-time outage proportional to the size of `posts`. This is a real, diff-grounded operational concern about migration safety/availability, not an application correctness bug per se.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The embed retrieval is fire-and-forget: the controller enqueues RetrieveTopic and renders 'loading', whose only follow-up is a 30-second document.location.reload() in app/views/embed/loading.html.erb, so an import that can never succeed leaves the visitor in an endless reload loop with no error state ever rendered. A user on a page whose import fails (dead/moved embed_url, fetch error, unparseable content, DB rejection) sees 'Loading Discussion...' reload every 30 seconds indefinitely — each cycle re-enqueues a job and re-queries the DB — while neither the end user nor the operator gets a surfaced failure; the only trace is buried Sidekiq error entries, and the 60s Redis throttle key claimed by the first failed attempt (lib/topic_retriever.rb:26-28) makes intermediate reloads no-op 'successfully' before the loop retries.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a loading flow with no terminal failure state: `EmbedController#best` enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb` whenever `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil. The loading view unconditionally runs `setTimeout(function(){ document.location.reload(); }, 30000);`, so if retrieval/import never results in a `TopicEmbed` row (e.g., network/parsing failure in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` / `TopicRetriever#fetch_http`, or a permanent mismatch), the iframe will reload forever and keep re-hitting `embed#best`. Each reload re-enqueues `RetrieveTopic` again; the 60s Redis throttle in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` only reduces work inside the job, not the repeated enqueues or the endless reload UX.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] perform_retrieve runs the entire feed poll inline via Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) with no error isolation, so any feed error (unreachable SiteSetting.feed_polling_url, SimpleRSS parse failure, a crashing item) propagates out of perform_retrieve before fetch_http on line 45 ever runs, failing the RetrieveTopic job for an unrelated, perfectly valid embed_url. An operator who enables feed polling with a broken feed URL breaks interactive embedding for every new page on the site: each visitor's request enqueues a RetrieveTopic job that dies inside the inline feed poll, the direct HTTP import never executes, and all visitors are stuck in the infinite 'Loading Discussion...' reload loop.

adjudication.rationale: `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` unconditionally runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true (lib/topic_retriever.rb), with no `rescue`. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` does network I/O and parsing (`SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`) that can raise, so failures will propagate out of `perform_retrieve` and prevent the subsequent `fetch_http` call from running. Since `EmbedController#best` enqueues `:retrieve_topic` and otherwise renders `loading` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb + app/views/embed/loading.html.erb), a broken feed URL can prevent any new embeds from being fetched via HTTP and keep clients stuck reloading.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The rss.items loop has no per-item error handling, so the first item that raises aborts the entire feed import — most concretely, i.content is nil for feed items with no content element (plain RSS 2.0 feeds that use <description> only), and nil.scrub raises NoMethodError at line 35. One malformed or content-less item permanently halts processing of every item after it; with sidekiq_options retry: false (line 12) the hourly job never retries, so the enabled feed importer imports only a prefix (or nothing, on description-only feeds) each hour with no per-item record of what was dropped — and via TopicRetriever's inline call the same crash also fails every interactive embed retrieval.

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb the loop does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` with no nil-guard or per-item rescue. If `i.content` is nil for any feed item, `nil.scrub` will raise `NoMethodError`, aborting the entire job mid-feed. The job is configured with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so it won’t automatically retry. Additionally, TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline when `feed_polling_enabled?`, so the same exception can break interactive embed retrieval as well.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Every request to /embed/best for an unknown embed_url unconditionally enqueues a RetrieveTopic job with no rate limit — the only throttle is the 60-second Redis key "retrieved:<full embed_url>" inside the job (lib/topic_retriever.rb:26), which is bypassed by varying the path or query string while keeping the matching host and forging the client-controlled Referer header that is the sole gate in ensure_embeddable. An attacker (the route requires no authentication) exhausts Sidekiq workers and the outbound HTTP client: each unique embed_url variant performs a server-side open(url) fetch of the embeddable host and, when feed polling is enabled, a synchronous full-feed download and re-import (Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute) inside the job, stalling all background work including email processing.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a public route `get 'embed/best' => 'embed#best'` and in `EmbedController#best` it enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` whenever `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil, with no controller-level throttling. The only throttling shown is in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`, which keys on the full `@embed_url` string (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`) for 60 seconds, so varying query/path yields unlimited distinct keys and therefore unlimited jobs. The sole gate in `ensure_embeddable` is `URI(request.referer).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, and the Referer header is client-controlled/forgeable. Each job can perform server-side `open(url)` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` and, when `feed_polling_enabled?` is true, synchronously triggers `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` which downloads/parses the full feed (`SimpleRSS.parse open(...)`). This enables a practical Sidekiq/outbound-HTTP exhaustion attack as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] TopicEmbed.import writes unvalidated, unlength-capped external data into storage: embed_url is only presence-validated (line 6) against a varchar(255) column, and feed titles flow into Topic's title with skip_validations: true, so an embed URL over 255 characters (long query strings) or an oversized feed title raises ActiveRecord::ValueTooLong (or RecordInvalid on the null:false topic_id when creator.create returns an unsaved post) inside the RetrieveTopic job. Any embed URL longer than 255 characters permanently fails to import: the job crashes and retries forever while the visitor watches the eternal 'Loading...' reload loop; in the feed path the same overflow aborts the whole poll at that item.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `topic_embeds.embed_url` as a `t.string` (default 255 bytes) with only `validates_presence_of :embed_url` (no length validation) and creates records via `TopicEmbed.create!` in `TopicEmbed.import` without any rescue. `PollFeed` and `RetrieveTopic` both pass external URLs/titles directly into `TopicEmbed.import` / `PostCreator` with `skip_validations: true`, so oversized `embed_url` (or other DB-length-limited fields like `title`) can raise `ActiveRecord`/DB exceptions during insert/update and are not handled. In the embed flow this would keep `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` returning nil and the controller will continually render the reload-loop `loading` page while the job keeps failing/retrying; in the feed flow one bad item can abort the polling run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] TopicEmbed.import silently returns nil whenever the URL fails the http(s) regex — or when creator.create yields no post (lines 23-29) — with no log line and no error result, and poll_feed ignores the return value entirely. Feed items whose link is non-http vanish with zero diagnostics — including the poll_feed fallback url = i.id (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:33), which for Atom feeds is typically a urn:uuid:/tag: URI that always fails the regex: the operator sees feed polling enabled and the job green, yet topics for those entries never appear and there is nothing to debug.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import` the very first line `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` causes a silent `nil` return for any non-http(s) URL (app/models/topic_embed.rb). In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, the code explicitly falls back to `url = i.id` when `i.link` is blank or non-http(s) (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31-34), but then passes that `url` into `TopicEmbed.import` without checking the return value, so those items will be skipped with no diagnostics. Additionally, if `creator.create` returns no post, `import` also returns `nil` without logging. This is a real, diff-grounded behavior leading to dropped feed entries with no visibility.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] poll_feed silently returns when the configured SiteSetting.embed_by_username matches no user (typo, rename, or deleted account), after execute's settings guards have already passed. The operator who enables feed polling with a wrong username gets a completely no-op importer with zero feedback: the scheduled job 'succeeds' hourly, nothing is ever imported, and no log, error, or failure entry distinguishes this state from a working but idle feed.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `execute` only checks that `SiteSetting.embed_by_username` is present, but `poll_feed` then does `user = User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first` and immediately `return if user.blank?`. This matches the finding: a typo/renamed/deleted user yields a silent no-op with no log/error despite the settings guards passing. It’s an operational/observability gap rather than a functional defect under correct configuration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] feed_key — and the require 'digest/sha1' it exists to justify on line 4 — is referenced by nothing in the codebase; the feed-modified conditional-fetch/dedup logic it implies was never implemented. Dead-on-arrival code misleads the next maintainer into believing feed requests are deduplicated or conditional on a modification key; both the method and the require delete cleanly with zero behavior change, so the deletion test passes outright.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `require 'digest/sha1'` is only used by the `feed_key` method (`Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(...)`), and `feed_key` is not referenced anywhere else in the diff. The polling logic in `poll_feed` unconditionally does `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)` with no conditional-fetch/dedup based on that key, so `feed_key` (and the require) are currently dead code and can be removed without changing behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The disqus import loop now fetches each thread URL remotely through TopicEmbed.import_remote with no per-thread error handling, so the first dead or malformed link (OpenURI::HTTPError/SocketError from open(url)) aborts the entire import run, and non-http links silently return nil and skip that thread's posts. An operator importing a large Disqus forum loses every thread after the first bad link in a single command run — a failure mode introduced by this diff, since the previous code created the topic without any remote fetch.

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the import loop now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)` for each thread. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does `open(url).read` (and later `Readability::Document.new(...)`) with no `rescue`, so an `OpenURI::HTTPError`, `SocketError`, etc. will raise and abort the entire Thor task run. Additionally, `TopicEmbed.import` returns `nil` unless the URL matches `^https?://`, so non-HTTP(S) `t[:link]` values will be silently skipped, unlike the previous behavior which created a topic without fetching remotely.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The header if/else is closed with `<%- end if %>`, leaving a dangling Ruby `if` modifier that only parses because the ERB compiler splices the next emitted chunk (the blank-line buffer append) into the modifier's condition slot — a typo for `<%- end -%>` whose successful parse is an accident of compiler chunk layout. The header's conditional link renders only because a truthy output-buffer append happens to serve as the accidental condition, with the blank line emitted before the link instead of after; any edit near this line or an ERB engine that terminates scriptlet chunks with a statement separator instead of a following expression turns every /embed/best render into a template SyntaxError (a 500 inside every embed iframe), and no reader can reason about the current structure.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`, the conditional block is closed with `<%- end if %>` (no condition after `if`). That is not intentional Ruby and only compiles if the ERB handler happens to concatenate the next generated expression (e.g., an `_erbout << "\n"` buffer append from following whitespace) as the modifier condition. This makes the template fragile and potentially a SyntaxError depending on ERB/Erubi codegen or nearby edits; it should be `<%- end -%>`.
